summary: All seven acceptance criteria and four executor directives (D1-D4) verified against actual code. Every file cited in the plan exists with the required changes. D1 (the critical criterion) is fully met — both inputSchema and appendConfidenceEntry payload threading confirmed. D3 (no double emission) is clean: architect.ts owns the full instruction; phase-plan/index.ts has only a one-sentence pointer. Typecheck could not be re-run in REVIEWING phase (luca checks run is gated to execute/checks steps), but the executor-reported PASS and the absence of any TypeScript-incompatible constructs in the reviewed code gives high confidence.

criteria.description: schemas.ts: researchable JSDoc explains when to set true (factual, resolvable by automated research) vs absent/false (human judgment required); resolution JSDoc explains per-value meaning (auto=proceed, research=trigger research, ask=escalate). Both fields remain .optional().
criteria.evidence: packages/luca-core/src/confidence/schemas.ts:53-80 — researchable JSDoc at L54-64 explains 'Set true when the ambiguity is factual and resolvable by automated research … Leave absent or false when the decision requires human judgment'. resolution JSDoc at L66-80 covers per-value semantics: auto=proceed, research=trigger research, ask=escalate, and notes that absent → gate derives bucket. Both end with .optional() at L65 and L80.

criteria.description: D2: gate.ts resolution branch ends with compile-time exhaustiveness guard (const _exhaustive: never = entry.resolution) and still falls to ask. Helper remains pure.
criteria.evidence: packages/luca-core/src/confidence/gate.ts:51 — the else branch reads: 'else { const _exhaustive: never = entry.resolution; ask.push(entry) } // fail-toward-human'. The full resolution branch at L47-51 checks auto, research, ask explicitly, then exhaustiveness guard. Pure function: no IO, no side effects.

criteria.description: confidence.ts CLI: log subcommand has --researchable (boolean) and --resolution (string enum auto/research/ask) flags, threaded into payload; gate --help states {auto,research,ask,counts}.
criteria.evidence: packages/luca-cli/src/commands/write-surface/confidence.ts:139-151 — researchable flag (type: 'boolean') at L139-145, resolution flag (type: 'string') at L146-151. Threading at L195-199: conditional spread of researchable and resolution into payload (mirrors reviewHint pattern). Gate command description at L280-287 states output shaped '{ auto: [...], research: [...], ask: [...], counts: { auto, research, ask } }'.

criteria.description: D1 (CRITICAL): luca-confidence-log.ts inputSchema includes researchable: z.boolean().optional() and resolution: z.enum(['auto','research','ask']).optional(); both are threaded into the appendConfidenceEntry payload (not just declared in schema). This is the critical criterion — without payload threading, CLI flags are no-ops.
criteria.evidence: packages/luca-cli/src/write-surface/handlers/luca-confidence-log.ts:96-110 — inputSchema contains 'researchable: z.boolean().optional()' at L96-103 and 'resolution: z.enum(["auto","research","ask"]).optional()' at L104-110. Payload threading at L155-160: conditional spread of researchable (L155-157) and resolution (L158-160) into the entry passed to appendConfidenceEntry, mirroring the existing reviewHint conditional spread at L152-154.

criteria.description: D4: execute.ts confidence schema block now includes researchable? and resolution? (or points to luca confidence log --help).
criteria.evidence: packages/luca-tools/src/artifacts/modes/execute.ts:146-147 — the schema block at L133-149 now includes 'researchable?: true | false, // planning-time hint: factual ambiguity resolvable by automated research' and 'resolution?: "auto" | "research" | "ask" // planning-time gate-routing override (see luca confidence log --help)'. Both lines are present, preventing execute-mode schema drift.
